scope: GDT872 descriptive raw-group directed profile only; no rerun or mutation.
assessment: The primary distal within-paragraph rates are 51/529 = 0.096408 and 66/646 = 0.102167; the diagnostic rates are 9/91 = 0.098901 and 6/40 = 0.150000. Including cross-paragraph strata, primary distal is 53/583 = 0.090909 forward versus 72/705 = 0.102128 backward; diagnostic is 9/97 = 0.092784 versus 9/48 = 0.187500. Thus the data do not show a distal overall forward excess.
Near within-paragraph counts are 36/291 = 0.123711 forward versus 16/336 = 0.047619 backward. This is a descriptive near-band asymmetry, not an unobserved replication of the distal profile.

The profile does not demonstrate a persistent state or a reset mechanism: it measures directed whole-form adjacency opportunities, without an independently coded state, owner, item, or semantic endpoint. Local clustering, formula composition, anchor exposure, and unequal denominators remain compatible explanations.

Cross-paragraph strata are sparse: primary distal has 2/54 forward and 6/59 backward hits; diagnostic has 0/6 and 3/8. Calling these too sparse for a stable cross-boundary conclusion is justified, while zero or low cells do not refute a general boundary mechanism.

Same-side and opposite-side margins are not interchangeable with conditional concordance. For primary distal within-paragraph, same-side is 29/51 forward and 29/66 backward; diagnostic is 3/9 and 1/6. These margins share the opportunity denominator but do not control anchor or response exposure.
claim_ceiling: Descriptive raw-group profile; no semantic direction, persistent state, reset, translation, significance, or binary falsification.
implementation_note: The initial draft validator/producer defects were corrected before the PASS receipt; they are not scientific observations from this profile.
